verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Roof photos (pages 5-13) show a flat poured-concrete terrace surface bounded by a low parapet wall, with no tiles, sloped planes, or metal sheeting visible anywhere.
verdicts.rationale: Multiple photos of the roof surface clearly show a flat RCC terrace, consistent with the designer's answer.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_notes: The skylights and west side headroom and east side parapet wall are the obstructions that could affect the solar installation
verdicts.photo_observation: The Shadow Analysis diagrams (pages 19-21) explicitly show the east-side parapet wall casting shadows on the panel array between 9-11 AM year-round, and the west-side headroom structure casting shadows on the first 1-2 rows of panels in the afternoons across most months. The site layout also shows the headroom block sitting directly adjacent to the panel field.
verdicts.rationale: The designer's own notes list skylights/headroom/parapet wall as obstructions, and the shadow-analysis renders confirm real shading impact from the parapet wall and headroom on the array — directly contradicting the literal 'No' answer.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: The ballast mounting-stand render (page 19) shows a shallow, low-profile tilt across the row of pedestal stands (roughly 0.43m to 1.18m stand heights over a ~2.8m module run), consistent with a shallow single-digit-to-low-teens tilt typical of ballasted flat-roof racking.
verdicts.rationale: The schematic stand-height profile is consistent with a shallow ~10° tilt, though there is no direct protractor/angle measurement photo to confirm the exact figure.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: The site-layout top-view diagrams (pages 17-21) show a single contiguous flat roof section containing the entire proposed PV array; no second array or separate roof plane appears anywhere in the documentation.
verdicts.rationale: All panel layout diagrams show only one roof/array area.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 19's 3D render clearly shows individual cylindrical ballast/pedestal feet supporting each rail under the panels — no rafters, wooden beams, or MS angle-frame legs are visible.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?

verdicts.rationale: The schematic includes a compass reference, but its rotation relative to the tilted array isn't clear enough to confidently confirm true south-facing orientation.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Color-coded cable-routing overlays trace a continuous path across 8 consecutive photos (pages 10-17): a run along the roof parapet (red/green lines) descends through a wall penetration (page 12), continues along the corridor at the equipment-room level (pages 13-14) with visible white PVC conduit housing the cable bundle, terminates at the Inverter/ACDB/DCDB/Battery block and an earthing point (page 15), and separately the Solar Meter connects to the Main Meter inside the panel board (page 16, purple AC-cable line) alongside DC/AC/LA earth pits (pages 16-17). No overlay line dead-ends without reaching a labeled equipment/pit icon, and no unexplained line-color or thickness change occurs mid-run.
verdicts.rationale: The documented (proposed) routing forms one continuous, logically connected path from the rooftop array through to the metering and earthing points, with physical conduit visible at every exposed section — no orphan ends or inconsistencies found.
